justification: B uses sans headings against a serif body, a boxed abstract, running header and footer bands, a cover page, and a navy chart with an in-image title. Paragraph spacing is airy and consistent. Its drawbacks are a mostly empty cover page and an abstract whose labels sit on separate lines. A is a plain Times-style paper with tight indented paragraphs, no running bands, and a black bar chart. It is clean but dense and generic.

A is five pages and ends on a full page 5, while B spills a lone table onto a mostly empty page 6 (B6). B's numbered headings are confusing: English and Arabic headings are numbered separately, so the TOC reads "1 ... 2 ..." with the numbers misplaced in the Arabic lines (B2). A's TOC is clean, with bold English entries and aligned page numbers (A2). A's sans-serif headings and body text are consistent, whereas B mixes a serif body with sans headings. Both designs repeat the same KPI and table blocks and use the same header/footer bands.

A uses bold sans headings that stand out from the serif body, giving clear hierarchy (A3, A4). It fits the content on 5 pages, with no stranded table. B has weak, light-weight headings, a heavy top band, and an orphaned table alone on page 6 (B6) that is mostly empty. Its Arabic text is larger than its English, which is slightly inconsistent. A has misaligned heading indents, a rule that extends past the margin on A3, and some Arabic/English size mismatch.

Design B's blue palette keeps the donut-chart percentages legible (B6), while in A the dark navy slices make the dark labels nearly invisible (A6). B's sans-serif headings and large KPI figure give a clearer hierarchy and a more modern look (B2). B's blue charts also read better than A's all-black bars and pie (A3, A4). A's top rule and serif headings look elegant, but its charts are heavier and less readable.

A keeps one body size and a consistent left edge. Numbered headings sit clearly above the text, and the running header and footer bands add structure (A2-A5). B makes the first paragraph of each section larger than the rest, which reads as arbitrary and breaks the rhythm. Its headings are outdented from an indented body, so the left edge shifts, and the rules above headings add clutter (B2-B4). The tables and charts are about equal in both. B's centred-left cover is fine, but A's centred cover is tidier.

B has a strong navy title band on the first page with the abstract directly below. It adds running header and footer bands with page numbers, and its body text is consistent and easy to scan. A spends its first page on a mostly empty cover with a small title. It also mixes a larger first paragraph with smaller following ones, which looks inconsistent and makes the rhythm uneven. A's body text is justified with heavy hyphenation. The tables and chart are comparable in both designs.

Design B is a compact 4-page paper with a title band, running header and footer bands, and the table and chart sit together with the text. Design A wastes space: the cover page is almost entirely empty, the abstract sits alone on a mostly blank page, and the chart is stranded on its own page with a large void below it. Pages are left half empty (A2, A3, A6, A8). B has some awkward hyphenation and a heading split across a page break, but it reads far more continuously.

A has a strong navy title band, a boxed abstract, ruled section headings, running headers and footers, and a navy chart with a title, giving a clear hierarchy and a modern look. B is a clean academic layout with numbered headings, captions and tight indented paragraphs, but it is plain, with no bands. B's chart is black and its page 2 ends with a large gap. A's body text is light and the small table caption is not bold, but overall A is more polished and navigable.

A has navy header and footer bands with running titles and 'Page x of 6' (A2-A6), numbered headings, and larger Arabic text that is easier to read. B has no bands and a plain footer. B's Arabic is small, and its rules and headings are misaligned: the rules overhang and the heading and body indents differ (B3, B4). B's table of contents also drops the section numbers (B2). A ends with a nearly empty page holding a single orphaned table (A6), which is a weakness, but B has similar orphaned tables and KPI blocks split across pages.

A uses a refined serif with a navy palette. Its Arabic text is generously leading and fully justified, and its page footers are minimal. B justifies the English text, which opens uneven word gaps, and its Arabic body is smaller and denser. B's running headers and footers add clutter, and the page number sits off-center. Both share the same structure, including the orphaned table on the last page.

B is the more cohesive and complete document. Its header and footer bands carry running titles and 'Page X of 5' labels (B2-B5), and its pages are filled evenly. The sans-serif type is consistent between Latin and Arabic, and the body text is justified. A's last page (A6) is almost empty with only an orphaned table. A's serif headings pair awkwardly with the Arabic face, and its thin top rule gives less structure. Both designs repeat the same content, and the KPI and table styling is nearly identical. B's page 3 breaks the Arabic paragraph at the foot, which is a minor flaw, but B is still better overall.

A pairs a serif title with Arabic that matches the English in size, so the bilingual headings feel balanced (A3, A4). B's Arabic body and heading text is noticeably smaller and cramped, and its Arabic headings are weak (B3, B4). B's sans headings with blue KPI numbers look modern, and its table is slightly more colourful. But B's headings sit left of the indented body text, which is misaligned, and the rules extend unevenly past the right margin (B3, B5). A has an orphaned table on page 6 that is mostly empty, which is a flaw (A6), but B repeats tables just as redundantly. Overall A is more cohesive and legible.

A opens with a strong navy title band and puts the abstract and introduction on the first page. Its section headings are set off by blue rules, which gives clear structure (A1, A2). B spends a whole page on a mostly empty cover (B1), so the document runs to 5 pages with underfilled pages and large gaps at the bottoms (B2, B3). B's serif body is comfortable to read and its numbered headings are clear. A's light sans body is a bit thin, and its hyphenation is heavier. Tables and chart are nearly identical in both (A3, B4).

A has solid navy header and footer bands with page-of-total numbering, which give a clearer frame (A2, A3). Its sans headings contrast well with the serif body, and its numbered headings are clearer in the TOC. A's TOC numbers are awkward in the Arabic rows, though. B's serif headings are less distinct from the body, and its thin-rule header and footer feel weaker (B3). Both share the same layout flaws: a repeated KPI/table block and an orphaned table on the last page (A6, B6).

B keeps the scope list whole on page 1 (B1), while A splits it across pages, leaving an orphaned 'b. Consent service' at the top of A2. B's bold sans numbered headings are stronger and easier to scan than A's light serif headings with a rule above each one, which feels fragmented. B's running header and 'Page 2 of 2' footer are a nice touch. B has a flaw: the awkward 'Decem-ber' hyphenation in Next Steps (B2). A has a tidier title and stat layout, but the list split and the heavy rules hurt its flow.

B's pie and donut charts are oversized and clipped: the '26.6%' and '26.1%' labels are cut off, and the donut's dark-on-navy percentages are nearly illegible (B3, B4). B's Figure 5 area chart is squashed flat (B4). A's charts are well sized and every label is legible (A3-A6). A's summary has a strong KPI hierarchy with a big $84.2M figure. B's header and footer bands and its three-column KPI row are tidy, but they cannot make up for the broken charts. The two appendix tables are about equal.

A uses bold geometric headings that stand out clearly against the serif body, and its TOC is clean (A2). It has no header or footer bands, and its margins are slightly inconsistent: headings sit left of the body text and the rules run wider than the text (A3, A4). B's navy header and footer bands add a polished frame, but its numbered headings are lighter and weaker in hierarchy. B's TOC also puts the numbers awkwardly in the Arabic lines (B2). B ends with an orphaned table alone on a mostly empty page 6 (B6), which hurts its balance and rhythm. A fits the content onto fewer pages with a steadier flow.

A spreads 8 pages with large empty areas: the abstract sits alone on A2, the chart is stranded on A6 apart from its table on A5, and the last lines spill onto A8. Its mixed-size lead paragraphs are inconsistent. The dark cover (A1) and header rules are polished but cost space. B is a compact, coherent paper with numbered headings, abstract and title on one page, and the table, figure and captions together on B3. Numbered references match the citations. The text is dense and conventional but reads well.

A gives each chart room and keeps the labels intact. Its serif type and large KPI on the summary page feel elegant, though page 2 is half empty. B's pie and donut charts are oversized, with the 26.6% and 26.1% labels clipped (B3) and the donut percentages barely legible (B4). B also squeezes Figures 4 and 5 into short strips. B's header and footer bands add structure but crowd the pages. A's donut labels are also low contrast, but the charts are cleaner overall.

A uses bold sans headings with numbering, so the section hierarchy is clear. Its scope list stays together on page 1 and the running header and footer help navigation. B has light, small serif headings that look weak, and a rule above every section makes the page feel busy. B also splits the scope list across pages, leaving 'b. Consent service' orphaned at the top of page 2. B's tables are fine but its heading contrast is weaker.

B's bold numbered sans headings over a serif body give clearer section hierarchy than A's light-weight headings, and the sections stay evenly spaced without rules between them. A has rules above every section, which add clutter. Its stat row crowds the summary text, and the full-width header band on page 2 is heavy. A also hyphenates 'e-commerce' awkwardly. The tables are almost identical, and B has a minor 'Decem-ber' break.

A has header and footer bands with running section titles and 'Page x of 6', which aid navigation (A2, A3). Its bold sans headings and justified body text are easier to read, and the numbered headings tie into the table of contents. The numbering is clumsy in the Arabic lines, where it sits beside the title. B is cleaner and more elegant, but its light serif headings are weak, its hyphenated body text is awkward, and its footer is minimal. Both share the same content problems, including the stranded table on the last page (A6, B6).

Design B has a cleaner, more consistent layout. Its content is aligned to a shared left margin, and the numbered headings are easy to follow. Design A scatters rules between sections and uses odd indents, so the heading sits left of the body text and the content is pushed right. A also orphans item 3 of the scope list at the top of page 2. B keeps the scope list whole on page 1, and its page 2 starts with a clean heading. Both have similar tables, but B's margins and rhythm are more even.

A adds navy header and footer bands with page numbers, which give a polished, consistent frame (A2-A5). Its sans-serif body is cleaner and its Arabic is larger and more legible. B's Arabic text is smaller, and the serif body with sans headings feels less cohesive. B's headings are bold and clear, but its section rules and indents are inconsistent. Its rules overshoot the right margin on B4 and B5. B's TOC page numbers also disagree with the pages the sections actually fall on. A's TOC has an Arabic page-number mismatch too, and both designs repeat the same content blocks, so the tables and KPI rows are about equal.

A mixes a larger lead paragraph with smaller body paragraphs in every section, and the indented text with full-width rules looks inconsistent (A2, A3, A5). B uses one body size and numbered headings. Its running header and footer bands and full-width chart give a steadier, more readable page (B2-B4). A's left-aligned title cover is stylish, but the interior is less coherent.

A uses a refined serif for headings and a lighter, cleaner TOC with page numbers only. B adds numbered headings and the TOC numbering is garbled in the mixed Arabic/English rows (e.g. '2 كلمة...' and '4 أبرز...' placed oddly). B's heavy header and footer bands feel more intrusive, though they add navigation. The tables and KPI blocks are nearly identical, and both share the content problem of repeated blocks and an orphan table on the last page.

Design B gives each chart its own page, so the figures are clean and legible. Its pie has properly sized labels (B4), and its serif body with numbered headings reads well. Design A packs charts densely onto pages, and its pie and donut labels are oversized and clipped. The '26.6%' label is cut off by the West label, and '26.1%' is truncated (A3). The donut percentages are dark on navy and unreadable (A4). B's donut has the same unreadable-label flaw (B7), but it is smaller there. A's Summary band is a stronger header, but B's pages leave a lot of empty space below the charts.

A's bold sans headings and blue KPI figures give clearer hierarchy and a stronger header band (A1). Its Scope of Work list breaks after item 2b, leaving 3 alone on page 2, and the 'Dece-ber' hyphenation is a flaw. A's body text and rules are also offset from the heading margin, which looks slightly unbalanced. B is clean and consistent, but its light serif headings are weaker. B also splits the scope list mid-item, and a stray rule at the top of page 2 looks odd (B2). B's tables are as good as A's.

A has a navy header and footer band with running titles and 'Page X of 5' (A2-A5), so the pages feel finished and navigation is clear. Its TOC page numbers match the content, with Performance Highlights on p.3. A has 5 pages and fills each more evenly. B ends on a nearly empty page 6 holding one orphaned table (B6). B's TOC says Performance Highlights is on p.4 for the Arabic entry, which looks inconsistent. B's serif type is elegant and its spacing is airy, but it has only a thin top rule and a small footer, and the extra page weakens the whole. A's page 3 text runs tight to the footer, and its Arabic Performance Highlights paragraph splits across pages 3 and 4, which is a minor flaw.

B packs two figures per page, but its pie and donut charts have oversized labels that clip ('26.6%' and '6.1%' are cut off, as seen on B3), and the donut labels are low-contrast on B4. The charts in B are also squashed (B2, B4). A gives each figure its own page with clean, legible charts and numbered headings that make the hierarchy clearer (A2, A4). A leaves a lot of empty space on its chart pages (A3, A5, A6), and its donut percentages are also low-contrast (A7). Overall A is more polished and readable.

B is the tighter document. Its navy header and footer bands frame every page, and the page counts are consistent ("Page x of 5"). Content fills the pages evenly. A ends with an orphaned table alone on page 6, with the rest of that page empty. A's page 5 also ends on a stat row that is cut off from the table that follows it. A's TOC lists page numbers that do not match its pages (Performance Highlights is listed as 3 but its Arabic text sits on page 4). B's TOC has similar mismatches, but its Arabic text splits across pages 3 and 4, which is a flaw. A's serif type looks elegant, but its bands are thin and its layout feels more fragmented.

A opens with a strong navy title band and puts the abstract right under it. The running header and footer bands give clear orientation, and the body text is a consistent size. B spends page 1 on a mostly empty cover. Its first paragraph in each section is larger than the rest, which looks inconsistent. Its headings sit flush left while the body is indented, which looks awkward. The table and chart are comparable in both designs.

A uses a serif body with bold numbered headings, so the sections are easy to find. Its paragraph spacing is comfortable and it breaks cleanly between sections, with no orphaned fragments. B has a strong title band on the first page, but its light-weight headings are weak. It also splits paragraphs across pages (B1 to B2, B2 to B3, B3 to B4), and the rules above each heading add clutter. A's separate cover page is sparse but tidy (A1). Tables and charts are nearly identical in both.

A is compact and continuous: the title band and abstract share page 1, running headers and footers aid navigation, and the table and chart sit together on A3 with text flowing around them. B wastes pages: the cover is mostly empty, the abstract sits alone on a mostly blank B2, and the chart is isolated on B6 under a large void. B also has inconsistent first-paragraph sizing, with a larger lead paragraph followed by smaller text. B's serif type is elegant, but its page balance and rhythm are weaker.

Design B's charts are rendered cleanly, with pie and donut labels intact and a consistent one-or-two-charts-per-page rhythm. Design A's pie and donut labels are oversized and clipped (A3 '26.6%' is cut off by the slice edge, '6.1%' loses its first digit) and the donut percentages are nearly illegible (A4). A's pages are also crowded, and Figure 5 is squashed. A does have stronger structure: a banded Summary header, a KPI row, and running header/footer bars (A2). B's summary page is half empty (B2) and its pages carry extra whitespace, but its serif body with sans headings reads better and its figures are more trustworthy.

A is a compact, coherent paper: title, abstract and numbered sections flow together, and the table and figure sit with their captions (A3). B wastes pages: a mostly empty dark cover (B1), an abstract alone on a page (B2), and a chart stranded on a near-empty page (B6). Most B pages are half blank, so the document feels fragmented. B's section rules and abstract box are tidy, and its table is clean (B5). But the lead paragraph in each section is oddly larger, the chart has no caption, and the equation font is mismatched (B4).

Design B flows continuously, so each page is well filled. The chart sits right beside its table (B4), and the bold sans headings contrast clearly with the serif body. Design A leaves large empty areas: the abstract stands alone on A2, the chart is stranded on A6, and the references spill onto A8. A's dark cover is striking, but its headings are weak and light. B's heading indents and the inconsistent left alignment of the headings against the body text are minor flaws.

A keeps a consistent left margin, with headings, body text and tables aligned. Its sections hold together and the Scope of Work list finishes on page 1, so page 2 opens cleanly on Timeline. It also has a running header band and a clear footer. B indents the body relative to its headings, which looks misaligned. B orphans list item 3 at the top of page 2 and leaves "December" hyphenated onto a line of its own. B's bold sans headings against serif body text work reasonably well, but the cover band is a flatter, brighter blue.

A has a consistent left margin: headings, body and rules all align, and the table spans the full text width. The navy band and serif headings feel cohesive. B has headings outdented from an indented body, which leaves a ragged, unbalanced left edge. B also has a hyphenated 'Decem-ber' orphan in Next Steps and an e-commerce break in the summary. A's 3.4x stat row is slightly clearer. A's top rule on page 2 is a small oddity, and both designs split the Scope list across pages.

B puts two charts on each of pages B3 and B5, so the pages are fuller and the pacing is steadier. A gives each chart its own page (A3, A5, A6), which leaves large empty areas below the charts. A's three-up KPI row on A2 is tidy, and its header and footer bands add structure. But in A the donut labels on A7 are unreadable, dark text on navy. B's donut labels on B6 are also dark on blue, but they are legible. B's KPI layout on B2 is oversized and unbalanced, with a lot of empty space below. B's lighter blue is easier to read, and its running footers are quiet and do not compete with the content.

A uses bold numbered section headings with a serif body, so the hierarchy is clear and the page reads in a classic way. B has light, thin headings that are weaker than the body text and a rule above every section, which feels repetitive and crowded. B's dark header band on page 2 is a plus. A has a hyphenated 'Decem-ber' orphan on A2, while B breaks 'com-merce' and 'in-cludes'. Tables are similar in both.

A packs content into 5 pages, with running header and footer bands and bold sans headings that set a clear hierarchy. The table and chart sit together on A4 and flow continuously. B spreads the same content over 8 pages with large empty areas (B2, B3, B4, B6). The chart is stranded alone on B6, and the first paragraph after each heading is oddly larger than the rest. The dark cover in B is striking, but the body pages feel sparse and inconsistent, and the Limitations paragraph splits across B7 and B8.

A uses a sturdier serif with justified English text and larger headings, so section titles read more clearly (A3, A4). Its running headers carry section names, which helps navigation. B has lighter, thinner type, and its hyphenated body lines ("chan-nels") read less cleanly. B's Arabic is justified with wide word gaps, though its thick top band is a consistent touch (B2-B5). Both share the same flaw of a near-empty last page holding only a repeated table (A6, B6).

A has a cover page, a boxed abstract, rule-topped sans headings and a blue chart, so it looks more finished and the sections are easy to find (A1, A2, A4). Its first paragraph in each section is oversized, which makes the body text uneven. Its references have no numbers. B is a plain, consistent academic layout with numbered headings, numbered references, and figure and table captions, but the black chart is flat and the layout is plain. Page 2 of B ends with a gap at the bottom (B2, B3).

A ends on a nearly empty page 6 holding one orphaned table (A6) and has a half-empty page 3 bottom. Its TOC numbers headings, and the Arabic entries read oddly (A2). B is denser and more evenly filled across five pages, with no orphan page, though its Arabic section splits across pages 3 and 4 (B3, B4). B's headings are lighter, so its hierarchy is slightly weaker, but its pagination is better and the TOC cleaner.

B has a navy title band, a boxed abstract, rules above section headings, running headers and footers, and a navy chart with a title, so it reads as more polished and navigable (B1, B3). A is a clean, conventional paper with justified serif text and numbered headings. Its black chart is plain, and page 2 leaves a large gap at the bottom (A1, A2). B's light-weight section headings are somewhat weak and the abstract labels sit on separate lines, but overall B is more refined.

A keeps the Scope of Work list whole on page 1 and starts Timeline on page 2 with a running header band. B splits the list mid-item (2a on B1, 2b and 3 on B2), which breaks the flow. A's bold sans title and KPIs are stronger, though its hyphenated justified text is a small flaw. B's serif is elegant and its table spacing is slightly roomier, but the split list and the unbalanced page 2 start weigh against it.

Design A pairs a bold geometric sans heading with a serif body. Its blue chart palette is lighter and the area chart is clearer. On A6 the donut's dark percentage labels stay legible on the mid-blue. In B6 the dark labels almost vanish on the near-black segments, a real readability flaw. B's navy cover and top rule are tidy, but its charts are heavy and its small body text on B4 and B6 is hyphenated awkwardly (other-/wise). A's running footers are section-based, which is a reasonable choice.

A uses a consistent serif with clear headings, and the Arabic is legible and aligned with the heading rules (A3, A4). B's Arabic has glyph issues (a '?' appears in place of a character, e.g. 'نموا؟' on B4 and B5), and its Arabic paragraphs are small and dense. B's headings are misaligned, sitting left of the indented body text and with rules overhanging the right margin (B3, B4, B5). A's last page holds only a stray table (A6), which is a weakness, but B's pages are more crowded and have the same duplicated blocks.

B keeps all three scope items together on page 1 (B1), where A orphans item 3 at the top of page 2 (A2). B's left edge is consistent, and its page 2 has a running header band and footer. A has a bold sans heading with serif body, which is a clear hierarchy, but its content is indented and misaligned with the headings, and the hyphenated 'Decem-ber' in Next Steps is awkward. B's headings are light-weight, which weakens hierarchy slightly.

A is a consistent academic layout: numbered headings, uniform justified body, and a clear abstract, with steady rhythm and a captioned table and figure (A3). B has a nice cover and a more colourful chart (B1, B4), but the first paragraph of each section is set larger than the rest, so body size jumps inconsistently (B2, B3, B5). The indented body against the flush-left headings and the rules between sections look uneven. The abstract box is loose, and the chart title takes the place of a caption.

A has a clear hierarchy: numbered headings, a KPI row of three equal cards (A2) and consistent header and footer bands with section names and page numbers. Its serif body text and sans headings pair well. Its weaknesses are that each chart gets its own page, which leaves about half of pages 3-7 empty, and that the donut labels on A7 are illegible. B pairs two charts per page (B3, B5), which gives a better rhythm. However, its KPI block is lopsided, with a huge $84.2M, and the Summary page is mostly empty (B2). B's headings are small and its bands are minimal, and its donut labels are also illegible (B6). Overall A's structure and navigation give it the edge.

Both share the same layout and content. B adds solid navy header and footer bands and a 'Page x of 6' footer, which frame the pages and aid navigation (B2-B6). Its sans-serif headings contrast better with the serif body. B's numbered headings are a mixed bag: the numbers help in the ToC, but the Arabic numbering is awkward. A has a lighter header and footer and a cleaner ToC with no numbers, but the page-5 and page-6 table orphan problem is identical in both.

Design B fills its pages with continuous content. The table and chart sit together on B4 and the sections flow with consistent numbered headings, so it reads as a finished document. Design A leaves A2, A3 and A6 mostly empty. The chart is stranded alone on A6 and the abstract is isolated on A2. A's dark cover (A1) is striking, but its heading sizes are inconsistent: the first paragraph under each heading is larger than the rest. B's running header and footer bands help navigation, though they are heavy. B's justified text shows some loose spacing, but it is still easier to read overall.

A splits the Scope of Work list across pages (A1 ends mid-list, A2 opens with 'b. Consent service'), which breaks the flow and leaves an orphaned fragment at the top of page 2. B keeps the whole list on B1 and starts the tables cleanly on B2. B also has a running header band and a 'Page 2 of 2' footer. A's serif is elegant and has more generous spacing, but B's sans-serif is more legible, and its header band and tighter rhythm read as more consistent. B's page 2 is somewhat empty at the bottom, but this is minor next to A's break.

B adds navy header and footer bands with running titles and 'Page x of 5', so it reads as a finished report. Its single sans family is consistent and its Arabic is larger and easier to read. Its tables are tidy, and its page-1 to page-2 TOC matches the real page numbers. A has stronger bold serif section headings, but its Arabic is smaller, its section rules and indents are misaligned (headings sit left of the body text), and its pages have no running header. A's TOC also lists wrong pages: Performance Highlights is listed at 3 and Operations at 4, so these are not reliably accurate. B's headings are lighter than A's, which weakens hierarchy slightly, and its Arabic text is cut across pages.

A uses a clean sans-serif, navy header and footer bands with 'Page X of 5', and an even flow across its 5 pages (A3, A4). A's TOC page numbers disagree with where the sections actually fall, but B's are also off. B's serif type and green accents look decent, but it runs to 6 pages and ends on a nearly empty page holding one orphaned table (B6). B's page 3 also leaves a gap at the bottom, and its header and footer are thin with no bands.

A has a dramatic hero KPI and packs two charts on page 3 and page 5, so the pages feel fuller. Its donut labels (A6) are dark grey on blue but still faintly legible. In B the donut percentage labels (B7) are almost invisible on navy. B's header and footer bands are heavy, and B gives each chart its own mostly empty page, leaving large dead space. B's numbered headings and three-KPI row are tidy, but the unreadable donut labels are a serious flaw.

A pairs a bold sans heading with a serif body, so heading levels are clear and the page rhythm is steady. Its content fits on 5 pages with no orphaned table. B uses a light serif for headings, which weakens hierarchy, and it spills a lone table onto a mostly empty page 6 (B6). B's running headers and footers are a plus. A's Arabic headings are right-aligned but its rules extend unevenly past the margin (A3, A4). B's layout is more consistent but has weaker hierarchy and the wasted last page.

A flows continuously over 5 pages with bold sans headings, a filled page and the table and chart together on A4 (the chart is in blue, close to the table). B spreads the same content over 8 pages, with large empty areas on B2, B3, B4, B5 and B6, and the chart is stranded alone on B6. B's dark cover band is striking and its top rule is consistent, but its headings are light and weak, and the resulting pagination is choppy. A's body text is somewhat dense, but its hierarchy is clearer.

A keeps one consistent left margin, with numbered headings that read clearly. Its scope list stays whole on page 1, and page 2 starts cleanly on Timeline. B indents the body against outdented headings, so the left edge looks ragged. B also splits the scope list, leaving item 3 orphaned at the top of page 2. B's rules above every heading add clutter, and its right margin is uneven. The tables are comparable in both designs.

A packs charts densely and its pie and donut labels are oversized and clipped: '26.6%' runs into 'West' and the South label loses its leading digit (A3, A4). A's page 4 also has a tiny area chart above a large donut, which feels uneven. B gives each chart room, keeps the labels in proportion and cleanly separated, and has a calm serif hierarchy with an even rhythm (B3-B6). B's summary page is sparse and its donut percentages are low contrast, but A has the same donut contrast problem. A's navy header and footer bands and KPI row are a plus, but they don't offset the broken chart labels.

A's elegant serif headings and large $84.2M KPI give a clear hierarchy (A2). It also pairs two charts per page (A3, A5), so pages are fuller. B leaves the lower half of nearly every page empty (B3, B5, B6) and spends one chart per page. B's header and footer bands are heavy but orderly, and its numbered headings help navigation, so the gap is modest. Both have the donut labels unreadable in dark-on-dark (A6, B7) and the same bare bullet list in the appendix (A7, B8).

A has a clean cover page, a boxed abstract, sans-serif headings with a navy accent and running header/footer bands. Its paragraph spacing makes it easy to scan, and the chart carries its own title and a coherent navy colour. B is a plain, dense Times layout with indented, tightly packed paragraphs. It does have a proper figure caption, numbered references and a good table. It also leaves a large blank area on page 2. A's flaws are that the table and chart split from their results text, and the chart has no figure caption.
